comments.author: @HomeownerBrief
comments.text: A lot of the "trapped" feeling traces back to one thing that usually gets skipped before closing. In most states a buyer can request the association's resale/disclosure package during a review window: the recorded CC&Rs and rules, the current budget, the reserve study (how well-funded the HOA is for big repairs), recent meeting minutes, any pending litigation, and an estoppel/resale certificate showing balances, planned special assessments, or open violations. That packet is generally where the surprise fees, the underfunded reserves, and the looming assessment show up, while you can still walk away, not after you are bound. It will not fix a bad HOA, but reading it usually turns "I had no idea" into an informed choice. Worth asking your agent which disclosures your state requires and how long your review period actually is.
